subject: AWS marketplace: duplicate usage-id flagging — payout at risk
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <billing@acme-corp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: billing+marketplace@acme-corp.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected duplicate usage IDs in AWS marketplace invoice (INV-ACME-202611)

Hi Irene,

Hope you're well. We're reconciling the November AWS marketplace invoice (INV-ACME-202611) and noticed multiple line items that reference the same usage identifier (usage_id) across different timestamps. That is causing our payable team to hold the payment — they flagged potential double-billing and are requesting an explanation or credit.

I've attached a short CSV extract (acme-usage-duplicate-lines.csv) and the invoice PDF. Key points:
- Two distinct invoice lines reference usage_id: 12345-ABCD on 2026-11-05 and again on 2026-11-12 with overlapping quantity.
- AWS purchase ID: amz-prod-0a1b2c3d (included in manifest).

Can Redwood confirm whether these are duplicate meter records on your side (seller metering id duplication) or an AWS aggregation issue? Our AP group needs a reconciliation note and either a credit memo or confirmation that one of the lines will be voided before they'll release payment.

We can expedite payment if we get a short confirmation and any evidence by EOD Wednesday (48 hours). Please loop whoever owns metering/ops.

Thanks,

Sarah Jones
Senior Billing Analyst — Acme Cloud Solutions
billing@acme-corp.com
Attachments: acme-usage-duplicate-lines.csv, invoice-ACME-202611.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <billing@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate usage IDs in AWS marketplace invoice (INV-ACME-202611)

Hi Sarah — thanks for flagging this and for the CSV.

Summary of what we see and next steps (proposed):
1) Immediate triage: Monica will pull Redwood seller-side metering logs for usage_id 12345-ABCD and the AWS purchase amz-prod-0a1b2c3d to determine whether two meter submissions were recorded from our endpoint.
2) AWS case: Jonas will open (or escalate) an AWS Marketplace case referencing the purchase ID and request their aggregation logs.
3) Finance/credits: Marcus will prepare a provisional credit memo template in case the duplication is confirmed; final credit depends on root cause.
4) Timeline: 48 hours for triage (target Wed 2026-12-01 EOD PT). If we can confirm a Redwood-origin duplicate, we will issue a credit memo and provide a short reconciliation note suitable for your AP.

Can you confirm: the AP contact and payment hold reference (bank/payment ref)? Also, please share the original manifest (if different from attached).

I'll follow up as we get the logs.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
Redwood Inference — redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate usage IDs in AWS marketplace invoice (INV-ACME-202611)

Adding initial findings after a quick look at seller metering logs:
- I can see two submissions with usage_id 12345-ABCD on 2026-11-05T14:02:13Z and 2026-11-12T02:45:07Z. Both entries came from the same upload endpoint but different batch IDs.
- Quantities differ (50 tokens vs 47 tokens) which is how the invoice shows two separate lines.
- Possible causes: retry duplication during a transient outage; or an idempotency key mismatch between our metering client and AWS.

Immediate asks for triage:
- Jonas: please raise AWS case with request for their consolidated metering/aggregation trace for the purchase id amz-prod-0a1b2c3d.
- Marcus: if we confirm seller-origin duplication we should draft a credit memo and communicate the ledger adjustment to the marketplace team.

I'll continue to collect the raw ingestion logs and will attach the seller-side manifest (acme-aws-purchase-manifest.json) when complete.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Marketplace Operations Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments pending: acme-aws-purchase-manifest.json

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Sarah Jones <billing@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 07:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate usage IDs in AWS marketplace invoice (INV-ACME-202611)

Thanks Monica — appreciate the fast triage. From finance perspective:
- If this is a Redwood-origin duplicate, we will issue a credit memo equal to the duplicated quantity amount and coordinate with Acme to apply it to INV-ACME-202611.
- If the duplication is on AWS's aggregation layer, we will coordinate with AWS but may need AWS to issue/confirm the correction. In that case, we will standby to apply credit once AWS confirms.

@Sarah — can you confirm whether AP will accept a Redwood credit memo (PDF + brief reconciliation) or if they require a corrected AWS invoice? That determines our parallel path (credit now vs wait for AWS).

Action items: Marcus to prepare provisional credit memo draft; Monica to provide seller logs; Jonas to open/track AWS case.

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks all — this is exactly the level of detail we need. AP confirmed they will accept a vendor-issued credit memo (PDF + reconciliation) to release the hold if it references the invoice number and shows the duplicated lines/amount.

We can approve immediate payment upon receipt of:
- Redwood credit memo for the duplicated quantity and total, and
- One-page reconciliation note (explain root cause and corrective steps).

I'll keep the AWS case on our side open in parallel but please prioritize the credit memo if it's straightforward — AP will expedite once the credit is filed.

Sarah Jones
Senior Billing Analyst — Acme Cloud Solutions
